practiceReport.name: Peter Woods
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Trench/box position (DT) — historically higher active rate through braced upper-body & ankle soreness (81% baseline).
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report
practiceReport.beatComment: Woods opened Week 11 prep with back-to-back full practices before having his reps limited Friday, which prompted the Chiefs to tag him as questionable. The rookie first-rounder has not been cleared by medical staff to play Sunday, so he will miss his third consecutive game due to a neck injury. Bryson Eason and Marcus Harris will continue to operate in rotational roles on the interior defensive line behind Chris Jones and Khyiris Tonga in the absence of Woods, whose next chance to play is Thanksgiving Day against the Bills.

practiceReport.name: Omarr Norman-Lott
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Trench/box position (DT) — historically higher active rate through braced upper-body & ankle soreness (81% baseline).
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report
practiceReport.beatComment: Norman-Lott was activated from the Chiefs' reserve/PUP list Wednesday, but he was limited in all three practices during Week 11 prep and drew the questionable tag for Sunday's game. He's in the final stages of his recovery from a torn ACL that he sustained in October of 2025, but he's not quite ready to make his return. Norman-Lott's next opportunity to make his 2026 regular-season debut is Thanksgiving Day against the Bills.

practiceReport.beatComment: VanSumeran injured his knee in the second half, and with no other fullback on the 53-man roster, the Chiefs could turn to tight end Jake Briningstool to provide additional blocking out of the backfield. VanSumeran's status over the coming days will be worth monitoring, given that the Chiefs are operating on a short week and play against the Bills on Thanksgiving Day.

practiceReport.name: Noah Gray
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Standard NFL positional availability baseline (78% Questionable conversion).
factors: Questionable tag adjusted by player career prior (78%)
practiceReport.beatComment: Gray's injury status was announced late in the game after Kansas City had already built an insurmountable lead, so it would be a surprise if the tight end returns to the contest. The bigger picture is the Chiefs' Thanksgiving matchup against Buffalo -- if Gray is dealing with a more-than-minor issue, his availability for that game could be in peril. Gray finished Sunday's matchup with three catches for 21 yards on five targets.

practiceReport.name: Nick Bolton
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Every-down starter workload (98% snaps) — 82% active conversion baseline when logging Limited Friday reps.
practiceReport.beatComment: Bolton popped up on the Chiefs' injury report with a shin issue Wednesday, but it doesn't look like it was anything serious. He's fifth in the league in total tackles (89) going into a Week 11 matchup versus a pass-happy Cardinals offense.

practiceReport.name: Jaydn Ott
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Perimeter speed/cut position (RB) — requires full deceleration/burst clearance on lower-body tags (76% Questionable baseline).
practiceReport.beatComment: Ott was unable to play against the Falcons in Week 10 due to a hamstring injury. However, the undrafted rookie out of Oklahoma was cleared to practice in full Wednesday, so he should be available for Sunday's home game against the Cardinals. If Kenneth Walker (groin) cannot play in Week 11, then Ott would have the opportunity to serve as the Chiefs' RB2 behind rookie fifth-rounder Emmett Johnson.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Jared Wiley
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Wiley was carted to the locker room in the first quarter of the Chiefs' Week 10 win over the Falcons with an ankle injury. The tight end will now be on IR as he nurses his fractured ankle until at least the latter part of the regular season. Travis Kelce, Noah Gray and Jake Briningstool are now the only tight ends on the Chiefs' active roster.
